newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress party polls to expose internal rifts.
newsitem.headline: India Congress party polls to expose internal rifts.

text.p: India's Congress party is poised to hold a triangular contest to find a new leader, in a rare election bound to expose sharp divisions within the nation's oldest political machine.
"There are three contestants in the field," Oscar Fernandes, polling officer for the election of the Congress party chief, told a news conference on Monday after the deadline for nominations.
A fourth candidate, A.R. Antulay, from the western state of Maharashtra withdrew his nomination for president late on Monday, Fernandes said.

If the candidates are unable to bury their differences and fail to arrive at a consensus, it will be only the third set of internal elections in the 112-year history of the Congress party, said Ved Prakash, a Congress leader.
Candidates can still step down before June 9, the date set for electing a new party chief, Prakash told Reuters.

Congress has ruled India for all but five years since independence from Britain in 1947, but has been hit by a string of scandals and suffered a crushing loss in general elections last year. It still provides vital support to Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling coalition.
"We hope finally a consensus will be arrived at and Sitaram Kesri will be elected as the party chief," a senior Congress leader, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Current Congress president Sitaram Kesri, 76, is being challenged by two younger leaders, Sharad Pawar and Rajesh Pilot, for the post.
Pawar and Pilot have launched a blistering attack on Kesri, accusing him of manipulating the organisational elections in which 8,000 delegates will cast their votes.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Pawar as saying: "I decided to contest the election as I wanted to bring in collective leadership which is now lacking in the party, decentralisation of power and more weightage to the sentiments of grassroot level workers of the party."
"I have been opposing Mr Kesri's selection and demanding election from the beginning. Why should I withdraw?" PTI quoted Pilot as telling reporters in eastern city of Calcutta.
"Mr Pawar has supported Mr Kesri for the last nine months. now suddenly he discovers that Mr Kesri cannot run the party," Pilot added.

Kesri, whose party provides key support to the ruling United Front, in April toppled then prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government by suddenly revoking its support, and renewed its backing only after the group changed its leader.
